AB03-q01-woawmv: Too early; wait until engine rpm is down close to idle before pushing in the clutch.
The clutch waits until rpm is close to idle, well after you start braking.
AB03-q02-n0fxjy: Locked wheels do not release trailer brakes; locked steering wheels cost you steering control.
Locked wheels slide; the real danger is losing steering control, not a shorter stop.
AB03-q03-1hwwpt: ABS works through normal braking pressure; spring brakes come from low air, not ABS.
ABS lowers pressure to a safe level; more pressure would lock the wheels.
AB03-q04-n2n71f: You may or may not stop faster with ABS; its benefit is keeping control and steering.
ABS can be on the tractor, the trailer, or both; any of these helps.
AB03-q05-ibowej: Tractor ABS keeps tractor wheels from locking; pumping is not the handbook method.
Tractor-only ABS does not control the trailer; watch it and let up if it swings out.
AB03-q06-w2nohk: Full pedal is allowed only in an emergency if you always drive vehicles with ABS on all axles.
Pumping is not the ABS technique; brake as always, using only the force needed.
AB03-q07-6jgpg4: Tractor ABS alone is not enough; you need working ABS on all axles of every vehicle you drive.
Trailer-only ABS does not qualify; it takes working ABS on all axles.
AB03-q08-211izc: ABS is an addition; when it fails you still have your regular brakes.
ABS failure does not trigger the spring brakes; those come on from low air pressure.
AB03-q09-7ix2pp: That describes stab braking; controlled braking avoids locking the wheels at all.
Controlled braking uses the brake pedal, braking hard without locking the wheels.
AB03-q10-1051cw: A 3-second application is the downhill braking technique, not stab braking.
Stab braking uses full braking and release, not rapid pumping while turning hard.
AB03-q11-fcs3fn: Reapplying too soon keeps the vehicle from straightening out; it is not about ABS turning off.
Spring brakes come on from low air pressure, not from early reapplication.
AB03-q12-l0dvdu: 3 seconds is the downhill brake application; wheels can take up to 1 second to roll.
½ second is air brake lag; wheels can take up to 1 second to roll.
AB03-q13-v7apfv: Seeing and recognizing a hazard is perception, not brake lag.
Brake lag happens before the brakes work, while air flows through the lines.
AB03-q14-3gn2lf: 3 seconds is the downhill brake application time; lag is ½ second or more.
Only hydraulic brakes work instantly; air brakes lag ½ second or more.
AB03-q15-ksnk9e: Brake lag distance is one of the 4 parts, so it is not the answer.
Perception distance is one of the 4 parts, so it is not the answer.
AB03-q16-i11vkf: 243 feet is the total at 35 mph; at 55 mph it is over 450 feet.
346 feet is the total at 45 mph; at 55 mph it is over 450 feet.
AB03-q17-ondeps: 61 feet is the reaction distance at 55 mph; brake lag adds about 32 feet.
142 feet is the perception distance at 55 mph; brake lag adds about 32 feet.
AB03-q18-wej5yl: Engine braking helps prevent fade; relying on the brakes too much causes it.
Proper adjustment prevents fade; out-of-adjustment brakes make the others overheat.
AB03-q19-ijukd7: The fade problem is heat: out-of-adjustment brakes quit working their share, overloading the rest.
Air use is not the issue; the other brakes overheat because they carry the extra load.
AB03-q20-52ajfx: Light steady braking all the way down is the wrong technique; brake to 35, release, repeat.
Don't exceed your safe speed; brake at 40 down to about 35 mph, then release.
AB03-q21-r34dnt: 1 second is how long stab-braked wheels may take to roll; downhill applications last about 3 seconds.
Applications last about 3 seconds, braking from safe speed to about 5 mph below it.
AB03-q22-myyz28: Don't wait for the spring brakes; they may take a long distance or skid you. Stop now.
Pumping uses up air; it does not build pressure. Stop and park as soon as possible.
AB03-q23-3kqyi3: Spring brakes come on, not release, as pressure falls into 20–45 psi.
ABS does not turn off spring brakes; they are slow because they don't work on all axles.
AB03-q24-g6co75: Parking brakes on very hot brakes can damage them; chock the wheels and let them cool.
Holding the pedal is not a parking method; chock the wheels on a level surface.
